summary: The non_gaia variant is a code-only Python implementation organized around models, service orchestration, and wrapper agent classes. It provides useful state models for containers and trucks and includes methods for monitoring full containers, truck status, overdue containers, and truck-load prioritization. However, it does not implement autonomous agent communication, the nearest-truck algorithm returns the first free truck, deadline handling is only a check, and prioritization is not integrated into task assignment.

findings.description: Container and truck monitoring are represented in the domain model.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/models/system.py:20-38 defines get_full_containers, get_warning_containers, get_free_trucks, get_busy_trucks, and get_full_trucks.

findings.description: The code contains an explicit truck-load prioritization helper.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/models/system.py:73-77 sorts trucks by current_load / capacity in descending order.

findings.description: The nearest-truck requirement is not implemented; the method returns the first free truck and ignores the container_location parameter.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/models/system.py:48-56 says it would calculate actual distances in a real system and returns free_trucks[0].

findings.description: The one-day collection requirement is checked but not enforced through assignment priority, escalation, or guaranteed dispatch.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/models/system.py:58-71 returns overdue container IDs, and container_monitoring_agent.py:14-27 adds them to attention lists, but task_assignment_agent.py:19-27 only resets a container when a truck is assigned.

findings.description: More-filled truck prioritization exists as a helper but is not used by the assignment path.
The implementation uses direct method calls and a central operation service rather than defined agent-to-agent messages or protocols.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/agents/task_assignment_agent.py:13-27 directly calls system methods and truck.assign_container; no send/receive or message contract appears in the agent classes.

findings.description: Debug-style print statements are used in runtime paths.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/main.py:15-19 prints success/error messages; operation_service.py also prints system checks and simulation output.

findings.description: Dependencies are range-based rather than pinned, reducing reproducibility.
findings.evidence: non_gaia/implementation_workspace/waste_collection_system/requirements.txt:1-4 uses crewai>=0.20.0, pydantic>=2.5.0, python-dotenv>=1.0.0, and pytest>=7.4.0.

missing_requirements: Actual nearest non-full garbage truck selection based on distance or location.
Autonomous communication from containers to the truck network or between truck agents.
Operational enforcement that a full container is collected within one day.
logical_inconsistencies: Agent classes import CrewAI Agent but do not subclass or instantiate CrewAI agents, so the implementation is closer to service-layer orchestration than a multi-agent system.
prioritize_trucks exists but the assignment flow bypasses it.
get_nearest_available_truck accepts container_location but does not use it.
implementation_risks: Dispatch choices can be geographically wrong because distance is not calculated.
Overdue containers may be reported but not acted on.
The absence of explicit message protocols makes multi-agent coordination behavior untestable and ambiguous.
Range-based dependency specifications can change behavior across installations.
